clue.text: Plant's trumpet something fine revolving, moreover

parts.note: to crow is to trumpet or boast about something
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: revolving turns the word for moreover round so it reads backwards

parts.note: moreover means too, as well

explanation.surface: A boastful aside about something splendid, with a twist, apparently about a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' acts on the word for moreover only. 'Plant's' is the definition plus a link 's (plant is).
explanation.definitionFit: A buttercup-family wild flower with leaves shaped like a bird's foot bears this name.

clue.text: House, splitting the expense?

indicators.note: splitting means breaking into the word for expense, so it sits inside

parts.note: cost means expense

explanation.surface: Sharing hosting duties and dividing the bill between two people.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: two hosts share the costs of a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as a joint host is to share the job, and often the bill, with someone else.

clue.text: Need month abroad convalescing

indicators.note: abroad means all over the place, scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A month away is needed to recover from illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovering from illness is idiomatically described as being on the way back to health.

clue.text: Courses for lovers flourish

parts.note: fans are lovers or devotees of something
fare is food, the courses of a meal

explanation.surface: Meals laid on for devotees, done with a flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourish' is a noun here: a burst of trumpets.
explanation.definitionFit: A flourish is a showy trumpet call announcing someone's arrival.

clue.text: What's turning up in odd bits of earthy clod?

definitions.text: What's turning up in odd bits of earthy clod?

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the picked letters read from bottom to top
odd bits are the first, third, fifth letters and so on of the two words

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at something colourful found in a lump of soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of EARTHY CLOD are ERHCO; 'turning up' reverses them. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-brown pigment is an earthy clay mineral that turns up in soil.

clue.text: Miss revolutionary struggle basically bottling it

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning right round, so the run of letters is read backwards
bottling it says the two words hold the run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A young woman's revolutionary struggle, essentially lost as she loses her nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottling it' looks like losing one's nerve; it signals that LEBASI sits across struggLE BASIcally, which 'revolutionary' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is a title for an unmarried woman, standing for any girl's name such as this one.

clue.text: Fish I didn't catch that's leaping for seed

indicators.note: in a down clue leaping means going upwards, so the pieces read from the bottom up

parts.note: tuna is a fish
eh? is what you say when you didn't catch something; the 's gives S

explanation.surface: Someone missed a fish jumping for a seed.
explanation.walkthrough: TUNA plus EH'S (eh? is said when you didn't catch something) is TUNAEHS; 'leaping' in a down clue sends it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut of the African shea tree is a seed yielding a butter used in cosmetics.

clue.text: Found rupees worth less

parts.note: to found an argument on something is to base it on that

explanation.surface: Discovering that some Indian money has lost value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' is the verb to found, not the past of find.
explanation.definitionFit: More base means lower in value, as base metal is worth less than gold.

clue.text: Float needs unusual biofuel: unknown quantity

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters are put into an odd new order

parts.note: y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A float that runs on an odd green fuel of uncertain amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring thrown to a person in the water keeps them afloat.

clue.text: A blow maybe to find green fragments on piping

definitions.text: A blow maybe to find green

parts.note: chips are small broken fragments
piping hot means very hot

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for green bits among hot pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: Green is a golf green; the blow is a stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a short lofted stroke is played to land the ball on the putting surface.

clue.text: Boot lined with heavyweight article kicks behind, just

indicators.note: lined with puts the following pieces inside the word for boot, like a lining

parts.note: to hoof a ball is to boot it, kick it hard
a ton is a heavy weight
the is the definite article
heels are kicks made with the back of the foot, as in rugby

explanation.surface: A boot reinforced with something heavy that kicks out behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boot' is the verb to kick, and the kicking word is split around the other three pieces; 'kicks' is also misleading, a noun for heel-kicks.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means following closely, only just behind someone.

clue.text: Get attendant to make escape

parts.note: to get a joke is to see it, understand it
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: Arranging for a servant to help someone run away.
explanation.definitionFit: Escape here is a noun for a slow leak, as of liquid or gas through a crack.

clue.text: Quietly stop gossip about uniting much of Middle East

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for stop reads backwards

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block
ana is a collection of anecdotes or table talk about a person

explanation.surface: A plea to hush the chatter about a political union across the region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns BAR and ANA together, giving ANARAB.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a movement aiming to unite all Arabic-speaking peoples of the region.

clue.text: Present judge harbouring intention to retire: I fear the worst!

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the whole assembly reads backwards
harbouring means holding the word for intention inside

parts.note: present means here, in attendance
an aim is an intention

explanation.surface: A judge, on hearing of someone's plan to step down, gloomily expects disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: HERE plus J holds AIM to give HAIMEREJ; 'to retire' turns that whole run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament prophet of doom gives his name to any habitual pessimist, whose cry this would be.

clue.text: Popular and gracious King keeps disapproving word for me

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
my! and gracious! are both exclamations of surprise
boo is a word that shows disapproval
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A well-liked, kindly monarch who still keeps a word of disapproval for the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gracious' is the exclamation, not kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces a personal opinion: as far as I'm concerned.

clue.text: Banned cricketer over his disastrous match performance

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for the cricketer reads backwards

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
a pair of noughts, two ducks, is a batsman's worst result in a two-innings match

explanation.surface: A cricketer banned after a dreadful showing in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns BAT into TAB. In cricket a duck is a score of nought, and scoring nought in both innings of a match is a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is forbidden by custom or rule is said to be off limits in this way.

clue.text: Fight to contain throng, one for a time making for hero's vehicle

indicators.note: one is I and a time is T, so I replaces T
to contain means the fight word holds the crowd word

parts.note: a battle is a fight
a mob is a throng, a crowd

explanation.surface: A superhero fighting through a crowd in his car, pressed for time.
explanation.walkthrough: BATTLE holding MOB is BATMOBTLE; 'one for a time' swaps the second T for I.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-book caped crusader drives a car named after himself.

clue.text: Fears American with power to gatecrash parties

indicators.note: to gatecrash is to get into a party uninvited, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: sects are factions or parties

explanation.surface: Worries that a powerful American will turn up uninvited at parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parties' means factions, not social gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect something is to fear or believe it without proof.

clue.text: Hamburger's accompanied by sandwiches girl opened

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between its parts

parts.note: a Hamburger speaks German, where and is und
Di is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl unwrapping a burger that came with a side of sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamburger' is a person from Hamburg, so the word is German.
explanation.definitionFit: Opened, as of a parcel or buttons, is the past tense of unfastening.

clue.text: One's drawers are being pulled out or up?

definitions.text: One's drawers are being pulled out or up?

parts.words: One's drawers are being pulled out or up?
parts.note: a chest has drawers pulled out; a theatre helper pulls an actor's underpants up

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a sideboard with drawers and a person who helps an actor into costume.

clue.text: Word that fits in Times Jumbo's sadly not British English

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters are put into a sorry new order

parts.note: T is time, so times gives two of them

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the British letter

parts.note: taken as written, with its S

explanation.surface: A grumble that the Times Jumbo crossword sadly lacks proper British English.
explanation.walkthrough: JUMBOS less B leaves JUMOS; with TT, 'sadly' rearranges them into MOTJUST.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means exactly the right expression for the occasion.

clue.text: Judge's rage put off juvenile a lot

indicators.note: put off means the word for rage is removed

parts.note: an umpire is a judge in sport
ire is rage
a teen is a young person

explanation.surface: A judge's fury puts a young person off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' is adverbial, matching the informal use: many times over.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means a great many, countless.

clue.text: Import from the Kensington area

definitions.meaning: W8 is the London postcode for Kensington, read out as the answer

explanation.walkthrough: Kensington is a district of west London whose postcode is W8.
explanation.definitionFit: Import and importance both mean significance or influence.

clue.text: Saw demonstrator confronting bishop

parts.note: one who proves or demonstrates something
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A protester standing up to a bishop, witnessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb; it is a noun, an old saying, and 'demonstrator' is not a protester.
explanation.definitionFit: An old saw is a traditional saying, a maxim.

clue.text: I felt that permit would be needed for small hooter

parts.note: ow! is a cry of pain
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A painful reminder that a licence is needed for a little horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl, which hoots, is a small one.

clue.text: Lead on in race, showing a bit of leg

parts.note: to hie is to hurry, race
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

explanation.surface: A runner taking the lead in a race while revealing some leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The bone of the hip joint is part of the upper leg's skeletal frame.

clue.text: Last in though you will feel so welcome

indicators.note: last in tells us to take the final letter in each of the following words

explanation.surface: Even if you arrive last, you will still be made to feel at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheery greeting on meeting someone serves as a welcome.

clue.text: Studiously ignoring Conservative with traditional bearing

parts.note: old means traditional, long-established
shouldering a load is bearing it

explanation.surface: A Tory with an old-fashioned manner, deliberately snubbing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone a deliberate snub is an idiom from turning one's back on them.

clue.text: Work, cutting length out of cross

parts.note: a saltire is an X-shaped cross, as on the Scottish flag

explanation.surface: Work on cutting a piece out of a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' looks like an instruction but belongs to the definition: a cutting, biting work.
explanation.definitionFit: A satirical piece is a written or staged work whose humour is sharp and wounding.

clue.text: Low-key function bridge players attend

parts.note: a do is a social function, a party
West and North are two partners at the bridge table
to be at an event is to attend it

explanation.surface: A modest party for which the bridge players turn up.
